findings.description: The instance user-data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. User data is retrievable by principals with instance/metadata access and is commonly retained in deployment state or logs, exposing reusable credentials.
TCP/22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0. Because the associated instance is launched in a subnet that assigns public IPs and routes to an Internet gateway, this exposes SSH to arbitrary Internet hosts.
TCP/80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 for the publicly addressed portal server, but no TLS listener or HTTPS-only control is configured. Traffic to the service can be intercepted or modified in transit.
The security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. A compromised portal instance can make arbitrary outbound connections, increasing command-and-control and data-exfiltration exposure.

The attached EBS data volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key. Its protection therefore depends on an external account-level default rather than this configuration, and it can be created unencrypted where that default is absent.
